result.markdown: --- title: Introduction to R, Day 2 author: "Ronald Geskus" engine: knitr format-links: - html toc: false number-sections: false webr: channel-type: "shared-array-buffer" cell-options: autorun: false message: true warning: true eval: true echo: false format: revealjs: slide-number: true logo: "figures/OUCRU.jpg" preview-links: true theme: solarized transition: fade show-slide-number: print embed-resources: true include-in-header: - text: | filters: - webr --- ## Learning goals {.smaller} - Day 1 - Basic structure of the R program and language - Use the RStudio working environment - Import, inspect and manage a data set - Select variables (columns) and rows (observations) - Missing data, factors, dates ::: {.fragment .highlight-red} - Day 2 - Using graphics in base R - Functions, packages - Object specific functions - Lists - Writing more transparent code ::: # Basic data visualisation ## R graphics systems: - Base graphics (package *graphics*) - Straightforward to use - Always loaded when R is started - See Ch.\ 12 of manual [An Introduction to R](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-intro.pdf){target="_blank"} ::: {.fragment} - lattice package. Less popular nowadays. Not covered here. - **ggplot2** package: Wednesday - Note: these systems cannot be mixed ::: ## Basic plot in base graphics {.smaller} Plot fare paid as function of age ```{.r} plot(titanic$age, titanic$fare) ``` Exercise: What would you like to change to make it good enough for publication? ::: {.fragment} - Formula based specification - basis for specification of regression models - general form: `dependent ~ independent` ```{.r} plot(fare ~ age, data=titanic) ``` - independent: variable names separated by operator (`+` for main effects and `*` for main effects plus interaction) - functions with formula (as first argument) have `data` and `subset` argument ::: ::: {.fragment} *Some possible changes: change labels along axes, rotate numbers along y-axis, add regression line, rescale fare* ::: ::: {.fragment} - Good summary on base graphics on page 5 of [Reference card](http://cran.r-project.org/doc/contrib/Baggott-refcard-v2.pdf){target="_blank"} ::: ## Arguments and parameters that can be changed {.smaller} - Within function only - `xlab`, `ylab`, `main` - `type` - `xlim`, `ylim`, `log` - Also via `par` function - `cex.axis`, `cex.lab`, `las` - `cex`, `pch` - `col`, `lty`, `lwd` - Only via `par` function - `mar`, `mfcol`, `mfrow` ## Some important functions for plotting ## - High level plot functions - `plot` - `hist` - `boxplot` - Low level plot functions (add to existing plot) - `points` - `lines`, `abline` - `text`, `legend`, `title`, `arrows`, `segments` ## Other plots 1-3. Plot fare paid as function of age, change scale, add regression line 4. Color points by passenger class 5. Make a separate plot by sex ::: {.fragment} Exercise 6: Make a histogram of age Exercise 7: Make a boxplot of age by passenger class. ::: ## Export: two types of formats {.smaller} - Vector format (pdf, eps, wmf, emf, svg) - digital image consisting of independent geometric objects (segments, polygons, curves, etc.) - can be enlarged without losing resolution - Raster format (png, jpeg, tiff, bmp). - rectangular grid of pixels, possibly with color - resolution impaired if image is enlarged - Graphics can be saved via the menu in the graphics/plots window, or a specific graphics file type can be created directly via code ```{.r} pdf("foo.pdf",...) ... dev.off() ``` or `win.metafile("foo.wmf",...)` or `png("foo.png",...)` and ending with `dev.off()` ## Aside: errors and warnings - Error: code cannot be executed; no output is produced ```{.r} 5 + "apple" titanic$age[1,5] ``` - Warning: something unexpected occurred; output produced, but potentially incorrect ```{.r} as.numeric(c("1", "2", "banana")) plot(fare ~ age, data=titanic, las=1, log="y") ``` # Functions and packages ## Basic format {.smaller .scrollable} - All actions are performed via functions: `sqrt`, `mean`, `help`, `library`, `t.test`, `plot` - Input: *required* and *optional* arguments; within parentheses, separated by comma - required: need to be supplied - optional: have default values Beware of sequence of arguments; required ones come first. Compare ```{.r} log(1000, 10) log(10, 1000) ``` ::: {.fragment} - Some functions have special "argument": `...` Meaning: anything that makes sense. Example: in `c` and `paste` function, which allow for the use of many values to - Output: result of calculations (typically assigned to R object), graphics, help window, etc. - You can use functions within other functions, e.g. `mean(c(3,6,8))` ::: ## Object specific functionality (I) - Output of function depends on *class* of object Examples: - `summary`: `summary.data.frame`, `summary.factor`, `summary.Date` default: `summary.default` - `plot`: `plot(y ~ x, data=..., ...)` Plot depends on class of `x`: scatterplot is default, but boxplot if `x` is of class factor and plot by year if `x` is of class Date ## Object specific functionality (II) Why important to know? - Finding information in help file - Very efficient in use. E.g. `plot` is a *generic function*, with specific methods depending on the class of the object that is the argument of the function. *We only need to remember `plot`* ## Functions: the inside {.smaller} - Function code can be seen by leaving out the parentheses \texttt{( )} ```{.r} IQR ``` - General structure: ```{.r} FunctionName(args) { lines of R code (collection of functions) } ``` The last value is returned as output - You can write your own functions: ```{.r} good.morning <- function(work){ if(work==TRUE) cat("wake up") else cat("you can stay in bed") } good.morning() ``` ## Packages {.smaller} - Regular R users transform recurring tasks into self-made functions - Can make it into a package, i.e. a collection of functions (and data): - [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/index.html) - [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org) - [WHO TB data](https://github.com/seabbs/getTBinR){preview-link="false" target="_blank"} - [AMR](https://msberends.r-universe.dev/articles/AMR/welcome_to_AMR.html) - [pharmaverse](https://pharmaverse.github.io/blog/posts/2025-02-28_theres_a_pharmaverse_package_for_that/managing-clinical-trial-data.html) - [SUSENAS](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/SUSENAS/index.html) - [vietnameseConverter](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/vietnameseConverter/index.html) - [sudoku](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sudoku/index.html) - [rStrava](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rStrava/index.html) - Give package developers appropriate credit and [cite their packages](https://ropensci.org/blog/2021/11/16/how-to-cite-r-and-r-packages/) ## Packages, where to find them? {.smaller} - [Comprehensive R Archive Network](https://cloud.r-project.org/web/packages/available_packages_by_name.html) (24504 packages on August 4, 2026) - [GitHub](https://rdrr.io/find/?repos=cran%2Cbioc%2Crforge%2Cgithub&page=0&fuzzy_slug=){preview-link="false" target="_blank"} (34867 packages on August 4, 2026) - [Bioconductor](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/BiocViews.html#___Software) - [Monthly Review Top 40 packages](https://rworks.dev/posts/june-2026-top-40-new-cran-packages/){target="_blank"} ::: {.fragment} - Need to be installed on your computer - R program itself also based on packages. Some loaded at startup *base*, *graphics*, *stats*, *utils* ... For example, *base* package contains `sqrt` function - Other packages need to be loaded before use, best way is via `library(pkg_name)` ::: # Some further topics ## Another object mode: list {.smaller .scrollable} - General mode to store information - Different modes cannot be mixed in vectors ```{.r} teachers <- c("Ronald","Hung","Tuyen") # mode character rooms <- c(306,306,305) # mode numeric c(teachers, rooms) # numbers become characters ``` - Modes can be mixed in a list: ```{.r} list(teachers, rooms) ## named list: list(teacher = teachers, room = rooms) ``` Two *components*, with names `teacher` and `room` - Data are of mode list, but with a special class `data.frame` ```{.r} mode(titanic) class(titanic) ``` ## Example: regression models How does fare paid depend on age? Linear regression: ```{.r} FareByAge <- lm(log(fare+3)~age, data=titanic) ``` Output: should contain everything to derive information from fitted model: coefficients, p-values, confidence intervals, residuals, ... Object of mode `list` and of class `lm`. Help file for summary: `summary.lm` ## More transparent (and often shorter) code {.smaller} - *formula* structure (regression models, `plot` function) - `with` function to save repetitive use of data set name : ```{.r} with(titanic, table(sex, survived)) ## instead of table(titanic$sex, titanic$survived) ``` - pipe operator `|>` (or `%>%` from the `magrittr` package) - combining functions in one line can make code obscure: `h(g(f(x)))` example: `round(proportions(table(titanic$sex,titanic$survived)),2)` - replace by `x |> f() |> g() |> h()` ## The apply functions - `apply`: apply a function over all columns or all rows of an array - `lapply`: apply a function over a list (including data.frame) - `sapply`: similar to `lapply` but more user-friendly if output can be coerced into a vector - `tapply`: can be used to split a vector in subgroups and apply a function to each of the subgroups - `aggregate` is an alternative to `tapply` ## Exercises - Make a summary of fare by passenger class using the `tapply` and the `aggregate` function - Fit the regression model that fits the mean fare paid (on the log scale) as a function of age: `FareByAge <- lm(log(fare+3)~age, data=titanic)` Summarize the results. What do you conclude? - Refit the model using 10 years as unit for age and summarize the results. Use the pipe operator, starting with `titanic |> transform(age=age/10) |> ...` Use a LLM if you get an error message ## Finding Information {.smaller} - Function `help`. R is object oriented! - Search on Google (use `language r:` if result is non-specific) - chatGPT or an R package such as [askgpt](https://github.com/cran/askgpt/){preview-link="false" target="_blank"} or [ellmer](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ellmer/index.html){target="_blank"} - [R documentation](https://www.rdocumentation.org){target="_blank"} [Rseek](http://rseek.org){preview-link="false" target="_blank"} - [R-universe](https://r-universe.dev/search){target="_blank"} - CRAN ([list with packages](https://cloud.r-project.org/){target="_blank"}, [Task Views](https://cran.r-project.org/web/views/){target="_blank"}, [FAQs](https://cran.r-project.org/faqs.html){target="_blank"}, Vignettes) - [Stack Overflow](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/r){preview-link="false" target="_blank"} - Have a look at the links provided in the appendix on the course website ## Exercise Find information on - descriptive statistics - change several categorical variables of a data.frame into factor variables - recognize nonstandard date formats

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
